# MCP Protocol Contract Requirements Checklist: Jisr MCP Server

**Purpose**: Validate that the MCP protocol, tool-contract, and adapter-parity *requirements* are complete, quantified, and consistent before implementation
**Created**: 2026-08-29
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Does the spec state a requirement for behavioural parity between the two MCP adapters, or does parity exist only as a plan-level decision? [Gap, Plan §Complexity Tracking]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the MCP protocol versions the server must support stated as a requirement, rather than implied by dependency choice? [Gap, research R3]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` values on filtered tool lists, or only for the risk they create? [Gap, research R5]
- [ ] CHK004 Is a tool deprecation and renaming policy specified, given tool names are required to be stable once published? [Gap, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for clients that do not support `outputSchema` or `structuredContent`? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-032]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the default page size specified, as distinct from the maximum? [Gap, Spec §FR-034]
- [ ] CHK007 Are requirements defined for how the error-code set is published and versioned for adopters? [Gap, Spec §FR-035]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the exclusion of Multi Round-Trip Requests from this read-only release stated as a requirement, or only as a research observation? [Gap, research R4]
- [ ] CHK009 Are requirements defined for tool-surface size relative to clients that limit how many tools they will load? [Gap, Coverage]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK010 Is "identical inputs, outputs, envelope, error codes, and safety annotations" given an observable definition for adapter and deployment parity? [Measurability, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the required content of server instructions specified, rather than described as "sufficient for an agent to understand"? [Measurability, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the human-readable summary accompanying each result given any length, content, or language requirement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-032]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "no client-specific code paths" defined precisely enough to be assessed — does adapter selection count? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003, SC-006]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the four non-success states given distinguishing criteria a client can act on, rather than names only? [Clarity, Spec §FR-036]
- [ ] CHK015 Is "opaque" defined for cursors in terms of what a caller must not be able to infer? [Clarity, Spec §FR-033]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK016 Is the `stale` state's presence in the contract consistent with a release where it is unreachable — is that stated deliberately? [Consistency, Spec §FR-036, FR-045]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the requirement that annotations be accurate sit consistently with the protocol's own position that annotations are untrusted hints? [Consistency, Spec §FR-037, research R6]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the tool names in the endpoint manifest, the tool contracts, and the spec identical in every case? [Consistency, contracts/endpoint-manifest.md]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the tool count consistent across spec, plan, manifest, and contracts, including the removal of the sync-status tool? [Consistency, Plan §Summary]
- [ ] CHK020 Do the envelope fields required by the spec and those documented in the contracts match exactly? [Consistency, Spec §FR-030]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK021 Does SC-006 define what counts as an "independent MCP client", and name the five? [Clarity, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK022 Is SC-002's coverage claim expressed so it can fail — is the divergence condition defined? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK023 Can SC-007 ("100% of results state source and freshness") be evaluated when only one source value exists? [Measurability, Spec §SC-007]
- [ ] CHK024 Are acceptance criteria defined for adapter parity, or is it asserted without a measurable outcome? [Gap, Spec §SC]

## Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK025 Are requirements defined for a client that caches a tool list across a change in the caller's authorization? [Coverage, Gap, research R5]
- [ ] CHK026 Are requirements specified for protocol-version mismatch between client and server? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK027 Are requirements defined for a tool result that exceeds a client's message size limit? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK028 Are requirements defined for cancellation or timeout of an in-flight tool call? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements specified for the transition when the v1 adapter is removed — notice, versioning, adopter impact? [Coverage, Gap, Plan §Complexity Tracking]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Is the assumption stated that part of the client ecosystem still requires the 2025-11-25 protocol, and is the evidence for it recorded? [Assumption, research R3]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the dependency on Node ≥20 traced to its cause and stated as a requirement rather than a consequence? [Traceability, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK032 Are the conditions for deleting the v1 adapter specified concretely enough to be acted on later? [Clarity, Plan §Complexity Tracking]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- CHK001 is the most consequential: adapter parity is load-bearing for the five-client promise but currently lives only in the plan, not the requirements
